title: Logged model search (search_logged_models): eager-load tags, params and metrics with selectinload, not per-model lazy loads
answers: Why does the logged models search (logged-models/search) take many seconds or hundreds of SQL round trips for one page?
When I add a new child collection to a logged model, how do I make search_logged_models load it without an N+1 query pattern?
Why does search_logged_models use selectinload instead of joinedload, and does eager loading change pagination?
Where are the tags, params and metrics of logged models loaded during a paginated search?
body:
Path: Paginated logged-model search (the UI logged-models/search call and SqlAlchemyStore.search_logged_models with filters, order_by, max_results and page_token) builds the main model query and then turns each row into an entity via SqlLoggedModel.to_mlflow_entity, which reads tags, params and metrics. The chokepoint is mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.search_logged_models.
Rule: Attach selectinload(SqlLoggedModel.tags), selectinload(SqlLoggedModel.params) and selectinload(SqlLoggedModel.metrics) as .options(...) on the paginated query, before .offset().limit().all(). Do not rely on the default lazy relationship, since each model then triggers its own SELECT and a page costs 3N+1 queries (about 300 for the default 100). selectinload runs as a post-load batch keyed by model_id, so the main statement keeps its filters, ORDER BY, OFFSET and LIMIT. joinedload would wrap LIMIT in a subquery, which is why it was avoided. Use the same pattern for any new child relationship read by to_mlflow_entity.
Symptom: On a large experiment (936 logged models with about 163k metric rows on PostgreSQL) the logged-models/search call took about 13.7s, while the database work was roughly 100ms. The cause was the round-trip count from per-model lazy loads of the three child relationships.
Constraints: Covers relationships declared without order_by; the batched and lazy forms return the same entity contents. Empty collections are still falsy, so the if self.tags else None branches in to_mlflow_entity are unchanged. Other read paths (get_logged_model, file store) are not covered by this change. A regression test, test_search_logged_models_eager_loads_tags_params_and_metrics in tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py, counts SELECTs with a before_cursor_execute listener and expects one per child table.
Applies: SQL tracking store search_logged_models and any paginated logged-model listing that serializes child collections.
applies: Paginated logged model search in the SQL tracking store (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL) when entities include tags, params or metrics.
says: The logged models search page takes many seconds to load on large experiments.
Loading a single page of models is very slow due to excessive database calls.
Improve page loading performance when viewing models with many parameters, tags, and metrics.
Browsing models in an experiment with hundreds of runs suffers severe loading delays.
search: SqlAlchemyStore.search_logged_models must eagerly load tags, params, and metrics using selectinload options on the paginated query rather than relying on lazy relationships. Lazy loading caused 3N+1 query round trips during to_mlflow_entity conversion, resulting in multi-second page loads on large experiments in PostgreSQL. The pattern avoids joinedload to prevent subquery wrapping of LIMIT and applies to SQL tracking store paginated search, excluding get_logged_model and the file store.
